lead.title: Mitotech takes its oral obesity pill MT-1101 head-to-head with semaglutide in preclinical data at ObesityWeek
lead.deck: The London biotech presented two invited posters on MT-1101 in Washington on Saturday, November 14: a once-daily oral treatment that drives weight loss by raising energy expenditure (speeding up mitochondrial fat-burning) rather than suppressing appetite. One poster measures energy expenditure and food intake in a diet-induced obesity model; the other compares MT-1101 directly with semaglutide on weight loss — no figures have been released yet. Billed as muscle-sparing and also aimed at MASH, the candidate is preparing to enter the clinic, and Mitotech plans to rely on pharma partners for late-stage development — one to watch as the market looks for mechanisms that complement GLP-1s.

milestone.title: Servier presents four-year results from the FIREFLY-1 trial of tovorafenib in pediatric low-grade glioma at SNO
milestone.summary: In children and young adults (6 months to 25 years) with relapsed or refractory BRAF-altered low-grade glioma, the once-weekly oral therapy OJEMDA (tovorafenib) shows a median time to next treatment of 50.9 months, up from 42.6 months at three years; among the 41 patients followed after stopping treatment, 76% stayed treatment-free for at least 12 months and 54% for at least 24 months, with no new discontinuations due to toxicity.
milestone.why: These exploratory data address the key question for pediatric targeted therapies: can treatment be stopped without rapid relapse? 54% of patients saw tumor rebound after stopping, but most of those retreated with OJEMDA saw their tumors shrink. Approved in the US under accelerated approval, the drug holds only an orphan designation in Europe — a comparable for European pediatric neuro-oncology biotechs.

brefsEurope.title: Novo Nordisk: CagriSema delivers about 21% weight loss at lower doses in the Phase 3 REDEFINE 9 trial
brefsEurope.summary: In 309 adults with obesity or overweight and no diabetes, the 1.7/1.7 mg and 1.0/1.0 mg doses of the GLP-1 + amylin combination produced 20.7% and 21.0% weight loss at 68 weeks among adherent patients (2.0% on placebo), with 2.9% and 4.9% discontinuing due to adverse events. Presented at ObesityWeek and published in The Lancet Diabetes & Endocrinology, the data raise the low-dose bar for European obesity biotechs, as the FDA is due to rule on the 2.4 mg dose in Q4 2026.

brefsEurope.title: Bavarian Nordic to lose CFO Henrik Juuel, who will step down at the end of April 2027
brefsEurope.summary: Juuel, who joined in 2018 and steered the vaccine specialist's finances through several acquisitions, is leaving for personal reasons; the board has started the search for a successor. Another change at the top, weeks after new CEO Tarja Stenvall took over.

brefsEurope.title: Klaria Pharma closes its rights issue at SEK 111.1M, 75% subscribed with the underwriter's contribution
brefsEurope.summary: Subscriptions covered 61.4% of the offering and underwriting by Vator Securities brought it to 75.3%; about SEK 37.3M is paid by set-off of claims, leaving roughly SEK 73.8M in cash before costs to shore up the balance sheet and execute the commercial strategy for its alginate film that sticks to the oral mucosa (migraine, cancer-related pain). Non-participating shareholders face dilution of about 43%.

brefsIntl.title: FDA declines, for now, to approve Summit and Akeso's PD-1×VEGF bispecific ivonescimab in EGFR-mutated lung cancer
brefsIntl.summary: The complete response letter (CRL) cites the lack of a significant overall survival benefit in the international population of the Phase 3 HARMONi trial, despite a progression-free survival gain; the HARMONi-3 trial against Keytruda is due to deliver first results by end-2026. A regulatory signal for the whole PD-(L)1×VEGF class, where BioNTech and BMS (pumitamig) are also in the race.

brefsIntl.title: FDA pauses its Commissioner's National Priority Voucher (CNPV) program, Reuters reports
brefsIntl.summary: Launched in June 2025 to cut some reviews to two months, the scheme has awarded 22 vouchers (slightly more than half of them leading to approval), mostly to big pharma, but none since Marty Makary resigned in May 2026; HHS says the program remains ongoing. One less fast lane for European biotechs targeting the US market.

word.definition: A hormone released by the gut when we eat that prompts the pancreas to secrete more insulin: the two main ones, GLP-1 and GIP, have become the basis of today's drugs for type 2 diabetes and obesity.

parts.label: GLP-1
parts.role: the star incretin: secreted by L cells in the gut, it stays active in type 2 diabetes and is the template for GLP-1 receptor agonists (semaglutide…)

parts.label: GIP
parts.role: the second incretin: produced by K cells in the upper gut, it is targeted either by activation (dual agonists such as tirzepatide) or by blockade (GIPR antagonists)

parts.label: Receptors
parts.role: the locks drugs aim for: they are switched on, blocked, or linked to another molecule to broaden the effect

how.t: Nutrients arriving in the gut trigger the release of GLP-1 and GIP into the bloodstream.
These hormones amplify glucose-dependent insulin secretion: in healthy people they are thought to account for about 50–70% of the insulin released after a meal.
GLP-1 agonists, then dual GIP/GLP-1 agonists, mimic and strengthen this signal; the new wave is testing combinations, oral forms and reverse approaches such as blocking the GIP receptor.

word.why: Incretins created the biggest market in pharma today, and the battle has moved to the second generation: weekly pills, better tolerability, muscle preservation, combinations. Europe has solid startups here, often born in the Danish ecosystem (Antag Therapeutics, Ousia Pharma) or backed by mega-rounds (Verdiva Bio, $411M Series A). Diligence point: against Novo Nordisk and Lilly — CagriSema still delivers about 21% weight loss at lower doses in REDEFINE 9 — a newcomer must prove a real differentiator, which explains the interest in complementary mechanisms such as Mitotech's.

startups.name: Antag Therapeutics
startups.use: AT7687, a first-in-class GIP receptor antagonist: first patient dosed in July 2026 in a 150-patient Phase 2a in combination with semaglutide (topline expected H1 2027); €80M Series A led by Versant Ventures.

startups.name: Verdiva Bio
startups.use: VRB-101, a once-weekly oral form of ecnoglutide (a GLP-1 peptide analog): enrollment in the Phase 2b EVOLVE-2 (200+ participants) completed in February 2026, results expected end-2026; $411M Series A co-led by Forbion and General Atlantic.

startups.name: Ousia Pharma
startups.use: University of Copenhagen spin-off developing a once-weekly dual-incretin + NMDA receptor antagonist conjugate designed to act on the brain's appetite centers; preclinical, seed round led by Omega Funds.
